world-politics.title: Trump Says Iran War 'Nearing Completion' but Vows to Hit Iran 'Extremely Hard'
world-politics.summary: President Trump addressed the nation from the White House, claiming core strategic objectives in Iran are 'nearing completion' while warning of two to three more weeks of heavy strikes. Oil prices surged and stocks fell as the mixed messages offered no concrete exit timeline.

world-politics.title: Iran's President Issues Open Letter Urging Americans to 'Look Past the Rhetoric'
world-politics.summary: Iranian President Pezeshkian released an unusual open letter in English addressed directly to the American public, questioning whether Washington is putting America first or acting as a proxy for Israel. The letter was seen as a sign of strength from Iran, pushing back against Trump's claims that Iranian military capabilities have been destroyed.

world-politics.title: Trump Suggests US Is Considering Leaving NATO, Calling It a 'Paper Tiger'
world-politics.summary: President Trump said in an interview with The Telegraph that withdrawing from NATO is 'beyond reconsideration,' escalating his criticism of European allies for not assembling a naval force to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. European leaders pushed back, with UK PM Starmer calling NATO 'the most effective military alliance the world has ever seen.'

world-politics.title: Israel Announces Plan to Occupy Southern Lebanon, Drawing International Condemnation
world-politics.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Katz declared Israel intends to occupy large parts of southern Lebanon in the strongest language yet since invading its northern neighbor. Lebanon's defense minister condemned the plans as 'a clear intention to impose a new occupation,' while Canada called it an illegal invasion.

world-politics.title: France and Japan Back Iran Ceasefire as European Coalition Weighs Military Options for Hormuz
world-politics.summary: French President Macron and Japanese PM Takaichi jointly called for a ceasefire in Iran and free passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The UK convened 35 foreign ministers to discuss diplomatic, economic, and potential military measures — with the US notably not invited to the coalition talks.

world-politics.title: NASA Launches Artemis II, First Crewed Moon Mission in Over 50 Years
world-politics.summary: NASA successfully launched the Artemis II mission carrying four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon — the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972. The launch from Kennedy Space Center marks a major milestone in NASA's plan to return humans to the lunar surface.

us-politics.title: Supreme Court appears likely to side against Trump on birthright citizenship
us-politics.summary: After more than two hours of oral arguments on April 1 — attended by President Trump himself — a majority of the Supreme Court appeared likely to rule against Trump's executive order ending birthright citizenship. Several conservative justices expressed deep skepticism toward the administration's argument that the 14th Amendment does not guarantee automatic citizenship to children of undocumented immigrants.

us-politics.title: Trump rails against birthright citizenship, courts after attending Supreme Court arguments
us-politics.summary: After attending Wednesday's historic Supreme Court arguments on birthright citizenship — the first time a sitting president has attended oral arguments — Trump lashed out at judges and justices who disagree with his policies, calling them 'stupid people.' The president's executive order would end automatic citizenship for children of undocumented immigrants and temporary visa holders.

us-politics.title: Trump gives prime-time address on war in Iran: Highlights
us-politics.summary: President Trump used a rare prime-time address to declare the U.S. is 'winning big' in Iran while warning he would hit the country 'extremely hard' over the next two to three weeks if no deal is reached. His mixed messages — simultaneously claiming objectives are 'nearing completion' and threatening further escalation — rattled markets, sending oil prices sharply higher.

us-politics.title: Congress plans to fully fund Homeland Security, leaders say
us-politics.summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson and Senate Majority Leader John Thune announced in a joint statement that Congress will fully reopen the Department of Homeland Security in the coming days, fund border security, and ensure all federal workers are paid. The bipartisan agreement commits to funding immigration enforcement and border security for the next three years.

us-politics.title: War powers measure to limit Trump's Iran authority fails in US Senate
us-politics.summary: A bipartisan resolution that would have required congressional approval before further US military operations in Iran failed in the Senate on a 53-47 vote, largely along party lines. Democrats argued Trump has circumvented Congress and offered inconsistent justifications for the conflict, while Republicans largely backed the president's war powers.

us-politics.title: Maryland Lawmakers Introduce 'No Kings Act' To Allow State Civil Actions Against Federal Officers
us-politics.summary: Maryland's General Assembly introduced HB 550 — dubbed the 'No Kings Act' — which would allow individuals to file civil lawsuits in Maryland state courts against federal law enforcement officers for alleged constitutional violations. The bill is part of a broader legislative movement across states pushing back against expanded federal authority and presidential immunity.

dfw-politics.title: Fort Worth ISD state takeover enters new phase with appointed board and superintendent
dfw-politics.summary: The Texas Education Agency's takeover of Fort Worth ISD moved into a new phase after the TEA named Dr. Peter B. Licata as state-appointed superintendent and convened the new board of managers for its first public meeting. The district of more than 70,000 students is now under full state control after years of failing academic performance, with the intervention expected to last up to four years.

dfw-politics.title: Texas smokeable hemp ban takes effect, hitting North Texas businesses hard
dfw-politics.summary: New Texas Department of State Health Services rules banning smokeable intoxicating hemp products — including pre-rolled joints and hemp flower — went into effect March 31, and North Texas hemp retailers are already feeling the impact. Licensing fees skyrocketed from $258 to $10,000 for manufacturers, and some DFW shop owners say 80% of their revenue was wiped out overnight.

dfw-politics.title: AT&T moving global headquarters from Downtown Dallas to Plano
dfw-politics.summary: AT&T announced it will relocate its global headquarters from its iconic Downtown Dallas tower to a new 54-acre campus on Legacy Drive in Plano, targeting partial occupancy as early as the second half of 2028. The move consolidates the telecom giant's offices from across the metroplex and marks a major shift for Dallas' largest Fortune 500 company.

dfw-politics.title: North Texas violent crime crackdown: Project Safe Neighborhoods expands to Dallas
dfw-politics.summary: Federal and local law enforcement officials are expanding Project Safe Neighborhoods from Fort Worth into northwest and northeast Dallas, targeting violent crime, drug trafficking, and illegal weapons. The initiative follows a deadly shooting at a Fort Worth park and focuses on repeat offenders, data-driven enforcement, and postal service interdiction of illegal drugs.

dfw-politics.title: Dallas Arboretum's 'Dallas Blooms' spring festival draws crowds through April 12
dfw-politics.summary: The Dallas Arboretum's signature spring event, Dallas Blooms, continues through April 12 along the shores of White Rock Lake, featuring the Southwest's largest outdoor floral festival. The spring season also brings the Texas Rangers home opener at Globe Life Field and a packed calendar of outdoor dining and arts programming across the metroplex.

dfw-politics.title: North Texas school voucher deadline extended after Islamic schools sue over exclusion
dfw-politics.summary: A judge extended the deadline for Texas' new school voucher program — which offers families up to $10,000 for private school tuition — after Islamic private schools and Muslim families sued claiming they were excluded on religious grounds. Those schools have since been added, but a new lawsuit seeks another extension as the dispute continues.

ai-news.title: OpenAI preps for IPO by year-end, tells employees ChatGPT must be a 'productivity tool'
ai-news.summary: OpenAI is aggressively orienting toward enterprise customers ahead of a potential IPO as early as Q4 2026, with CEO of Applications Fidji Simo declaring the company must convert its 900 million weekly active users into 'high-compute users.' The company has hired former DocuSign CFO Cynthia Gaylor for investor relations and is targeting $280 billion in annual revenue by 2030.

ai-news.title: OpenAI's next model 'Spud' reportedly nearing release in mid-to-late April 2026
ai-news.summary: OpenAI has completed initial development of a new model internally codenamed 'Spud,' with CEO Sam Altman telling staff that 'things are moving faster than any of us expected' and a release window of mid-to-late April 2026. The model features rebuilt audio capabilities, native multimodality, and what insiders are calling the company's first true 'AI Super App' experience.

ai-news.title: Google pulls ahead of OpenAI with stellar AI growth as Alphabet shares soar 80% year-over-year
ai-news.summary: Alphabet has transformed from an AI laggard into the market leader, with Gemini surpassing 750 million monthly active users and Google Cloud revenue up 48% in the latest quarter. Wall Street has notably shifted sentiment away from OpenAI toward Google, with Alphabet shares up over 80% year-over-year even as the company plans up to $185 billion in capital expenditures for 2026.

ai-news.title: Startup and venture investment in AI defence tech and infrastructure surges as of April 2, 2026
ai-news.summary: As of April 2, 2026, venture capital is accelerating into AI infrastructure, chips, autonomous systems, and defense technology rather than just applied AI products, with record-sized rounds and rising valuations reshaping the startup ecosystem. Capital is concentrating in frontier AI models, specialized semiconductors, and vertical solutions such as legal tech, healthcare, and enterprise automation.

ai-news.title: Nvidia's agentic AI push drives record inference demand as Jensen Huang eyes $3 trillion in revenues
ai-news.summary: Agentic AI systems being adopted at scale are fueling a major inflection in inference demand, benefiting Nvidia as it ramps Blackwell Ultra and prepares the Rubin chip for 2026. Jensen Huang has publicly raised the possibility of Nvidia becoming a $3 trillion revenue company, with analysts pointing to sovereign AI, enterprise AI, and physical AI as multi-trillion-dollar opportunities.

ai-news.title: Meta's 'Avocado' AI model delayed to mid-2026 amid competition from Google's Gemini
ai-news.summary: Meta has pushed back the release of its next-generation AI model, codenamed 'Avocado,' to at least May or June 2026 after internal tests showed it lagging behind Google's Gemini systems. The delay comes even as Meta ramps up capital expenditures to $115–$135 billion for 2026 and considers temporarily licensing Gemini technology for some products.

jpmorgan-chase.title: JPMorganChase launches 'American Dream Initiative' with $80 billion in small business lending
jpmorgan-chase.summary: JPMorgan Chase announced the American Dream Initiative (ADI) on March 31, pledging nearly $80 billion in small business lending over the next decade and a goal to expand its small business client base from 7 million to 10 million. The multi-year effort spans six focus areas: small business growth, housing affordability, financial health, careers and skills, healthcare, and local institutions.

jpmorgan-chase.title: Jamie Dimon says the American Dream is 'slipping out of reach' — and JPMorgan is spending billions to fix it
jpmorgan-chase.summary: Jamie Dimon warned that the American Dream is 'alive, but slipping out of reach for too many people' as JPMorgan unveiled its sweeping American Dream Initiative. The bank, which holds $4.4 trillion in assets, will accelerate investments in local communities while also hiring 1,000 additional small business bankers across its 5,000-branch network.

jpmorgan-chase.title: JPMorganChase to host Q1 2026 earnings call on April 14
jpmorgan-chase.summary: JPMorgan Chase will report first-quarter 2026 financial results on April 14 at 8:30 a.m. ET, with analysts closely watching net interest income guidance and Jamie Dimon's outlook comments amid a volatile geopolitical backdrop. The bank exceeded Wall Street profit forecasts in all four quarters of 2025 and in Q3 2025 reported EPS of $5.07 on revenue of $46.43 billion.

jpmorgan-chase.title: JPMorgan forecasts mid-to-high-teens jump in Q1 investment banking fees and market revenues
jpmorgan-chase.summary: At its February 2026 investor day, JPMorgan projected investment banking fees would rise by mid-to-high-teens percentage and markets revenue by a mid-teens percentage in Q1, easing investor fears about equity market volatility hurting deal pipelines. The bank maintained its 2026 annual adjusted expense forecast at $105 billion and confirmed Jamie Dimon will serve as CEO for several more years.

jpmorgan-chase.title: JPMorgan analysis: Trump tariffs cut US-China trade by 20% but tripled tariff costs for midsize firms
jpmorgan-chase.summary: A JPMorgan Chase Institute report found that aggressive 2025 trade policies successfully reduced outflows from midsize U.S. firms to China by approximately 20%, but at a steep cost — monthly tariff payments by those companies tripled compared to early 2025 levels. Firms are pivoting to Southeast Asia, Japan, and India as alternative suppliers rather than withdrawing from global markets entirely.

jpmorgan-chase.title: JPMorgan's 2026 outlook: Middle market resilient as tariffs become primary cost driver
jpmorgan-chase.summary: JPMorgan's Business Leaders Outlook report found that 71% of nearly 1,500 middle market executives remain optimistic about their company's outlook for 2026, with 73% expecting revenue gains — even as 61% report feeling a moderate-to-significant impact from tariffs. M&A activity is rebounding, with 39% of firms planning acquisitions in 2026, an 8% jump from the prior year.

dfw-events.title: Deep Ellum Arts Festival returns April 3–5, 2026 — Dallas's premier outdoor arts and music event
dfw-events.summary: The Deep Ellum Arts Festival takes over the vibrant Deep Ellum neighborhood April 3–5, featuring hundreds of visual artists, live music across multiple stages, food vendors, and community programming. It's one of the most anticipated spring events in Dallas and draws tens of thousands of visitors to the district each year.

dfw-events.title: Texas Rangers home opener vs. Cincinnati Reds at Globe Life Field — April 3, 2026
dfw-events.summary: The Texas Rangers kick off their 2026 home schedule on April 3 against the Cincinnati Reds at Globe Life Field in Arlington, with VIP Experience packages available. The series continues April 4 and 5, making Opening Weekend a must-see event for North Texas baseball fans.

dfw-events.title: Irving Margarita Festival at Toyota Music Factory — Saturday, April 4, 2026
dfw-events.summary: The Irving Margarita Festival returns to Toyota Music Factory on April 4 from noon to 6 p.m., featuring margarita tastings, live music, and a high-energy outdoor atmosphere. It's one of DFW's most popular spring day events, perfect for groups and families.

dfw-events.title: Scarborough Renaissance Festival opens for its 2026 season — Weekends April 4 through May 25
dfw-events.summary: The beloved Scarborough Renaissance Festival in Waxahachie opens for its 2026 run on April 4–5 and continues every weekend through May 25, transporting visitors back in time with live entertainment, artisan vendors, themed food, and interactive experiences for all ages. The festival is one of North Texas' longest-running spring traditions.

dfw-events.title: Winnipeg Jets at Dallas Stars — American Airlines Center, April 2, 2026
dfw-events.summary: The Dallas Stars host the Winnipeg Jets at American Airlines Center on Thursday, April 2 at 7 p.m. in a key late-season NHL matchup. With the Stars pushing for playoff positioning, this is a marquee home game for local hockey fans this week.

dfw-events.title: Fort Worth Main Street Arts Festival set for April 16–19, 2026 — One of the largest in Texas
dfw-events.summary: The Fort Worth Main Street Arts Festival, one of the largest arts festivals in Texas, returns to downtown Fort Worth April 16–19, featuring hundreds of visual artists, multiple live music stages, food vendors, and family-friendly activities. The free-admission event regularly attracts more than 200,000 visitors to the heart of Fort Worth.
